captions.instagram:
What is magnetism?

Iron filings trace invisible curves, a wire with current in it swings a compass, and a coil with an iron core lifts a car. Map fields in tesla, spin a motor, curl electrons in a magnetron, flip the Earth's field and heat a nail past 770 °C.

→ Unlike poles attract. Iron filings trace the field lines, running out of north and into south.
→ Ørsted, 1820: a current makes a field that circles the wire, and the compasses swing round.
→ Coil the wire and it becomes a magnet. Slide in an iron core and the field jumps hundreds of times.
→ Put a coil in the field and flip its current every half turn: a DC motor spins.
→ A magnetron’s 0.17 T field curls electrons past copper cavities, and out come 2.45 GHz microwaves.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/magnetismclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: What is magnetism? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Iron filings trace invisible curves, a wire with current in it swings a compass, and a coil with an iron core lifts a car. Map fields in tesla, spin a motor, curl electrons in a magnetron, flip the Earth's field and heat a nail past 770 °C.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/magnetismclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/magnetismclear

In this video:
• Poles, fields and the tesla. Like poles repel and unlike poles attract.
• Current makes a magnet. Ørsted found in 1820 that a current's field circles the wire, B = μ₀ I ÷ 2πr.
• A current in a field feels a push. F = B I L, at right angles to field and current (Fleming's left hand).
• Magnets in machines. A superconducting MRI magnet at 1.5–3 T, a magnetron's 0.17 T that curls electrons into microwaves, guitar pickups, transformers that trade volts for turns, and hard disks that store a trillion tiny magnets per square inch.
• Earth, hot iron and two myths. The Earth's field is tilted, wanders and has flipped many times; it shields us and lights the aurora.
